Question: The faces of each of two fair dice are numbered \(1,\) \(2,\) \(3,\) \(5,\) \(7,\) and \(8.\) When the two dice are tossed, what is the probability that their sum will be an even number?
Solution:
A sum of two integers is even exactly when both are even or both are odd. Each die has two even faces, \(2,8\), and four odd faces, \(1,3,5,7\).

The dice are independent, so the probabilities of the two disjoint cases are

\[
P(\text{both even})=\frac26\cdot\frac26=\frac19,
\]

\[
P(\text{both odd})=\frac46\cdot\frac46=\frac49.
\]

Adding gives \(\frac19+\frac49=\boxed{\frac59}\), choice \(\boxed{\text{C}}\). Only the parity of a face matters here, so there is no need to list every possible sum.
